v08-talay.name: Talay Şarapçılık
v08-talay.neighborhood: Alaybey — Çınar Çeşme Sok., town-centre shop
tags: Tasting counter, not a cellar tour
v08-talay.why: The island's oldest continuously family-run winery, pouring its own bottles at a town shop — not a tasting-room built for visitors.
v08-talay.verdict: The island's oldest family winery, pouring its own bottles at a town shop — not a tasting room built for visitors.
v08-talay.signature: A glass of crisp Çavuş white at the Meydan shop.
v08-talay.person: Founded 1948 by the Talay brothers — Necati, Hayati and Sebati; still a family firm.
v08-talay.caveat: A wine producer and sales shop, not a restaurant; the tasting counter, not the cellar, is what you walk into.
v08-talay._lane: At the cellar door — the island's own grapes

v02-corvus.name: Corvus Vineyards
v02-corvus.neighborhood: Alaybey — outside town, by the vines
tags: Cellar door — limited visiting days, check first
v02-corvus.why: The winery that put Bozcaada back on the world wine map in 2002 and remains its most decorated; the bottle that argues the island's own grapes can carry a serious wine.
v02-corvus.verdict: Not the island's oldest cellar — the one that put Bozcaada on the world wine map, and still its most decorated.
v02-corvus.signature: A flight of the indigenous Çavuş white and the Corpus red blend at the Wine & Bite shop.
v02-corvus.person: Reşit Söley — architect-turned-vintner; founded Corvus in 2002 and now makes 20-plus wines.

signal_chip.label: Jancis 17/20
signal_chip.full: Jancis Robinson scored Corvus Corpus 2004 at 17/20 — the highest Turkish score in her tasting
signal_chip.cosign: the bottle that proves the native grapes don't need Cabernet propping them up

v02-corvus.caveat: The estate opens to visitors only on limited days — check first. The Istanbul Wine & Bite bar has closed; taste here, not there.
v02-corvus._lane: At the cellar door — the island's own grapes

v06-amadeus.name: Amadeus Winery & Mozart Wine Bar
tags: Cellar door — bring your own transport
v06-amadeus.why: The convivial cellar door where the winemaker pours for you himself — not the famous name on the island, but the warm one.
v06-amadeus.verdict: Not the famous name on the island — the convivial cellar door where the winemaker pours for you himself.
v06-amadeus.signature: The Grillo white, paired with the island's vegetable and fish mezes.
v06-amadeus.person: Oliver Gareis — island-born Austrian; settled in the late 1990s and named the label for Mozart (founded 2010).

signal_chip.label: Katie Parla
signal_chip.full: Katie Parla recommends the Grillo as a meze pairing; Lonely Planet lists the vineyard
signal_chip.cosign: a convivial, engaging host worth the drive out

v06-amadeus.caveat: A small family operation outside town — taste and buy at the cellar door or the Mozart bar; you'll want your own transport.
v06-amadeus._lane: At the cellar door — the island's own grapes

v07-wednesday-market.name: Bozcaada Wednesday Producers' Market
v07-wednesday-market.why: Where the island's cheese and tomato jam are actually made — a producers' market in front of the castle, not the supermarket.
v07-wednesday-market.verdict: Skip the island supermarket — the Wednesday stall in the castle square is where the cheese and tomato jam are actually made.
v07-wednesday-market.signature: Local goat cheese and Ezine cheese, plus the island's signature tomato jam (domates reçeli).
v07-wednesday-market.caveat: Wednesdays only, in the castle square — a producers' market, not a daily one. Bring cash.
v07-wednesday-market._lane: La Rue — the market, the pastane and the roaster

v03-cicek-pastanesi.name: Çiçek Pastanesi Tahir Usta
v03-cicek-pastanesi.neighborhood: Çınar Çarşı — the square by Alaybey Mosque
v03-cicek-pastanesi.why: The island's sweet memory — additive-free dondurma from Bozcaada milk the supermarket freezer cannot fake; baking since 1959.
v03-cicek-pastanesi.verdict: The island's sweet memory — additive-free ice cream from Bozcaada milk the supermarket freezer cannot fake; baking since 1959.
v03-cicek-pastanesi.signature: Young-fig and mastic ice cream from island milk; damla sakızlı mastic-almond cookies.
v03-cicek-pastanesi.person: Run by Tahir Usta's children, the Günday family; the mastic-almond cookie traces to the island's Greek neighbours.

signal_chip.label: Katie Parla
signal_chip.full: Praised by food writer Katie Parla — 'still going strong'
signal_chip.cosign: the young-fig, lavender and almond ice cream is the one to chase

v03-cicek-pastanesi.caveat: A pastane and ice-cream counter, not a sit-down dinner spot. The best flavours are seasonal — figs and mulberries when the island's fruit comes in.
v03-cicek-pastanesi._lane: La Rue — the market, the pastane and the roaster

v09-kahverengi.name: Kahverengi Roastery
v09-kahverengi.why: An island-born specialty roaster that later opened in Nişantaşı — not an Istanbul brand parachuted in for the season.
v09-kahverengi.verdict: An island-born specialty roaster that later opened in Istanbul — not a city brand parachuted in for the season.
v09-kahverengi.signature: Hand-brewed filter coffee, no machine — beans the owners roast themselves.
v09-kahverengi.caveat: A coffee-and-pastry stop about a kilometre off the main square; no full menu, busiest April–October.
v09-kahverengi._lane: La Rue — the market, the pastane and the roaster
